import html # Example template; in real usage this would be defined elsewhere. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{post_heading}

{content}
{labels}
""" def render_blog_post(author_id: str, post_heading: str, content: str, labels: list[str]) -> str: """ Generate a secure, XSS‑protected HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- author_id : str Identifier of the post's creator. post_heading : str Heading/title of the user's post. content : str Primary content/body of the user's post. labels : list[str] Sequence of tags/labels associated with the post. Returns ------- str XSS‑protected HTML string representing the forum post. """ # Escape all user supplied strings to avoid XSS safe_author_id = html.escape(author_id, quote=True) safe_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=False) safe_content = html.escape(content, quote=False) # Wrap each escaped label in a element safe_labels = [] for lbl in labels: escaped_lbl = html.escape(lbl, quote=False) safe_labels.append(f'{escaped_lbl}') labels_html = " ".join(safe_labels) # Format the template with the escaped values html_output = USER_POST_FORMAT.format( author_id=safe_author_id, post_heading=safe_heading, content=safe_content, labels=labels_html ) return html_output.strip()
